RequestIdOut.description:
Correlation id for this response. Mirrors the request's
`X-Request-Id` when one was supplied; otherwise carries the
id Phoenix generated for this request. Use for log and
audit correlation.

IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key. Required on every `/v1`
write. The runtime dedupes retries by `(key, payload)`:
a duplicate key with a matching body replays the original
result, a duplicate key with a mismatched body returns
`409 Conflict`.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

RequestIdIn.description:
Optional client-supplied request correlation id. The
Phoenix endpoint generates a fresh id when this header is
absent. Whether client-supplied or server-generated, the
value is echoed back on the response as `X-Request-Id`
and written into the audit trail for this request.
RequestIdIn.name: X-Request-Id

BadGateway.description: Adapter or upstream provider returned a failure response. Treated as a caution-widening input (`retryable: false`); callers must not loop.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request body or missing required field.

Conflict.description: Idempotency-Key replay with a mismatched payload, or a state-machine conflict (e.g. approving an already-resolved decision, cancelling an executing intent).

Forbidden.description: Caller scope does not cover the subject (e.g. agent trying to read another agent's intent).

GatewayTimeout.description: Adapter or upstream provider did not respond in time. Treated as a caution-widening input (`retryable: false`); callers must not loop.

NotFound.description: Subject does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

NotImplemented.description: Endpoint is scaffolded but its owning engine has not landed yet. The body is the standard `ErrorEnvelope` with `code: "not_implemented"`.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Runtime is paused (global or scoped) and is refusing to advance execution. Callers must not retry into autonomy — the pause is lifted only by operator action.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request was structurally valid but a semantic guard rejected it (unsupported chain, asset not whitelisted by active policy, decision not currently `auto_exec`, …).

AddEvidenceRequest.description: Pin a new evidence artifact to a counterparty. Append-only: this endpoint never edits prior artifacts.
AddEvidenceRequest.title: AddEvidenceRequest

AddressLabelEntity.description:
Address label projected by
`CounterpartyJSON.address_label/1`. `retired_at` is non-null when
the label has been retired; retired labels are immutable.
AddressLabelEntity.title: AddressLabelEntity

AmountString.description:
Decimal amount as a plain string (no scientific notation,
no thousands separators). The `/v1` contract transmits amounts
as strings so JavaScript clients and scale-sensitive asset
math do not silently round through 64-bit floats. Example:
`"250.00"`.
AmountString.title: AmountString

ApprovalActionRequest.description:
Shared body shape for the approve and reject endpoints.
`actor_id` is required — it is captured on the successor
envelope and every audit event. `reason` is optional and is
persisted to the audit trail; reject paths typically set it.
ApprovalActionRequest.title: ApprovalActionRequest

ApprovalActionResponse.description:
Unified approve / reject response. `decision` carries the
successor envelope; `dispatch` discriminates the branch:

  * `"recorded"` — approve path, emitted with a `next_step`
    hint pointing at the execute endpoint. v0.1 does not
    auto-dispatch after approval — the operator must follow
    up with `POST /v1/decisions/{id}/execute`.
  * `"no_dispatch"` — reject path; the successor is a `block`
    envelope and nothing is scheduled.
ApprovalActionResponse.title: ApprovalActionResponse

ApprovalDecisionSummary.description:
Condensed decision view projected by
`BankWeb.API.V1.ApprovalController.summarize/1`. The field set is
deliberately narrower than `DecisionEnvelopeDetail` — queue
entries do not need the policy-snapshot reference or the
execution-plan list.

reasons.description: Decision-engine reason codes carried on the envelope.

ApprovalDecisionSummary.title: ApprovalDecisionSummary

ApprovalNextStep.description:
Operator-facing hint returned on the `"recorded"` dispatch
branch. Points at `POST /v1/decisions/{id}/execute` since v0.1
does not auto-dispatch after approval.

message.example: approval recorded; execute manually with smart_account_id when ready

ApprovalNextStep.title: ApprovalNextStep

ApprovalQueueResponse.description: List response returning every decision envelope currently in `approval_required`. The `decisions` array is unpaged today; a future issue may introduce cursor-based pagination.
ApprovalQueueResponse.title: ApprovalQueueResponse

Asset.title: Asset

AuditEventEntity.description:
Audit event projected by `AuditJSON.render_event/1`.
`correlation_id` is the intent id that ties related events
together across the runtime flow.

correlation_id.description: Intent id the event is correlated to, when applicable.

subject_id.description: Opaque id of the event subject. Typically a UUID; may also be a smart-account id or an on-chain address for non-intent subjects.

AuditEventEntity.title: AuditEventEntity

AuditListResponse.description: Paged audit stream. `next_cursor` is an opaque string; callers pass it back as `?cursor=...` to retrieve the next page.
AuditListResponse.title: AuditListResponse

CancelRequest.description:
Operator cancellation body. `reason` is required and is
persisted to the audit trail.
CancelRequest.title: CancelRequest

Chain.description:
EVM chain identifier. The schema permits additional values
so operators can extend the allowlist without a schema
change, but at runtime `/v1` v1 accepts only `"base"`.
Chain.title: Chain

ConnectSmartAccountRequest.description:
Browser-built smart-account connect payload. The three required
fields identify the smart account, the signer, and the chain;
`delegation_payload` is the signed delegation object from the JS
hook (see `assets/js/hooks/wallet_connect.js` and
`docs/wallet-connect.md`).

account.description:
Signer account address. The controller currently accepts any
non-empty string — format validation is intentionally loose
because `assets/js/hooks/wallet_connect.js` forwards
`accounts[0]` directly from the wallet, which is typically
an EIP-55 mixed-case EVM address (`0x` followed by 40 hex
chars with case-encoded checksum). The shared `EvmAddress`
schema's lowercase-only pattern would reject those payloads,
so this field intentionally does NOT `$ref` it. A future
issue may tighten this to a checksum-aware pattern once the
browser flow is fully signed.

chain_id.description: EIP-155 chain id. Currently accepted: `8453` (Base) and `84532` (Base Sepolia); other values are rejected with `422 unsupported_chain`.

delegation_payload.description: Signed delegation payload from the JS hook. Left as an open object; the shape is defined in `docs/wallet-connect.md`.

ConnectSmartAccountRequest.title: ConnectSmartAccountRequest

ConnectSmartAccountResponse.description:
Synchronous receipt for the connect request. The runtime
audits the request and enqueues
`Bank.Runtime.Workers.GrantDelegation` to dispatch the grant
to the adapter (#58 grant flow). The actual delegation row is
created asynchronously via the
`delegation.state_changed{state: "granted"}` callback path,
so a 202 here does NOT yet imply an active row — observe the
callback to confirm. The `note` field states this truthfully.

note.example: Grant request audited and enqueued. Observe the delegation.state_changed callback path for the granted artifact.

ConnectSmartAccountResponse.title: ConnectSmartAccountResponse

CounterpartyDetail.description:
Counterparty with preloaded active address labels, effective
trust assertions, and evidence artifacts. Produced by
`CounterpartyJSON.counterparty_with_preloads/1` on create /
update responses.
CounterpartyDetail.title: CounterpartyDetail

CounterpartySummary.description:
Counterparty fields projected by `CounterpartyJSON.counterparty/1`.
The list endpoint emits this bare object; single-counterparty
responses also carry preloaded associations (see
`CounterpartyDetail`).
CounterpartySummary.title: CounterpartySummary

CreatePolicyRequest.description:
Create a new policy rule. `rule_type` is required; `params` and
`scope` shape depend on the rule type and the decision engine
validates them at the context boundary.
CreatePolicyRequest.title: CreatePolicyRequest

DecisionEnvelopeDetail.description:
Decision envelope detail returned under the `data` key of
`GET /v1/decisions/{id}`. Mirrors the fields projected by
`BankWeb.API.V1.DecisionController.show/2` — including the
current-envelope flag, the supersession pointer, the policy
snapshot reference, and the current execution plan list.
DecisionEnvelopeDetail.title: DecisionEnvelopeDetail

DecisionOutcome.description:
Outcome written by the decision engine:

  * `auto_exec` — within policy, trust engine reports trusted,
    simulation healthy.
  * `hold` — permissions pass but something is temporarily off
    (stale simulation, cooldown window, trust re-check needed).
  * `approval_required` — sensitive trust, autonomy-tier
    threshold, or simulation flag routes to the operator
    approval queue.
  * `block` — terminal rejection; a new intent is required
    to retry.
DecisionOutcome.title: DecisionOutcome

DecisionShowResponse.description: Outer envelope around the decision detail. `data` carries the `DecisionEnvelopeDetail`; no other top-level keys are currently set.
DecisionShowResponse.title: DecisionShowResponse

ErrorDetail.description:
Inner error object carried inside `ErrorEnvelope.error`.

`code` and `message` are guaranteed on every non-2xx `/v1`
response. `hint`, `retryable`, and `details` are
opportunistic — clients MUST NOT assume they are present.
Absence of `retryable` means the caller has to decide from
the status code alone; it does NOT imply `false`.

`details` appears on 422 responses produced by changeset
validation: a map from field path to the list of error
messages for that field.

details.description: Optional; only present on 422 responses produced by changeset validation. Maps a field path (e.g. `"scope.amount_ceiling"`) to the list of error messages for that field.

hint.description: Optional operator-facing remediation hint. Some paths set this to `null` explicitly; callers should treat `null` and absence as the same signal.
hint.example: Retry with a fresh Idempotency-Key or resend the original payload.

message.example: Idempotency-Key reused with a mismatched payload.

retryable.description: Optional. Present when the controller opts in; absence does NOT imply `false`. When present, callers must not loop on `false`.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Outer response body returned on every non-2xx `/v1` response.
A single `error` key wraps an `ErrorDetail`; every reusable
error response in `BankWeb.OpenApi.Responses` references this
schema as its JSON body.

error.hint: Retry with a fresh Idempotency-Key or resend the original payload.
error.message: Idempotency-Key reused with a mismatched payload.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

EvidenceArtifactEntity.title: EvidenceArtifactEntity

EvmAddress.description:
EVM address as a lowercase `0x`-prefixed 40-hex-character
string. Used on the `/v1` contract only as the `raw_address`
fallback when no counterparty / label is known; raw addresses
always evaluate at trust `unknown`.
EvmAddress.title: EvmAddress

ExecuteDecisionRequest.description:
Body for manual execute. `smart_account_id` is required and
selects the delegation / smart account the adapter should sign
with. `reason` is optional and is persisted to audit; it
defaults to `"manual_confirm"` when absent.
ExecuteDecisionRequest.title: ExecuteDecisionRequest

ExecuteDecisionResponse.description: 202 response body: the newly enqueued execution plan under `data`, plus a fixed `status` tag used by the runtime as a step marker.
ExecuteDecisionResponse.title: ExecuteDecisionResponse

ExecutionPlanSummary.description:
Summary fields surfaced on execution plans by the `/v1/decisions`
endpoints today. Mirrors the keys produced in
`BankWeb.API.V1.DecisionController.show/2` and `execute/2`.

execution_status.description: Lifecycle state of the execution plan.

ExecutionPlanSummary.title: ExecutionPlanSummary

HealthDeepResponse.description:
Deep health probe payload returned by `GET /v1/health/deep`. Runs
every operational check in `Bank.Ops.Health.snapshot/0` (Postgres,
adapter reachability, stuck-plan count, …) and returns `503` with a
non-`"ok"` overall `status` if any check is degraded. `checks` maps
check name to a check-object whose required field is `status`;
individual checks may add fields additively.

checks.description: Map of check name to check-object.

HealthDeepResponse.title: HealthDeepResponse

HealthReadinessResponse.description:
Readiness probe payload returned by `GET /v1/health`. `status` is
`"ok"` when every check reports `"ok"` and `"degraded"` otherwise;
the endpoint returns `503` with a `"degraded"` body when any check
fails. `checks` currently contains only `database`, whose value is
`"ok"` on a reachable Postgres connection and `"error"` otherwise.

checks.description: Map of check name to status string.

HealthReadinessResponse.title: HealthReadinessResponse

Id.title: Id

IntentEntity.description:
The persisted intent record. Round-trips the submitted body
plus the lifecycle state, the runtime-assigned id and
`submitted_at`, the deterministic `payload_hash` used for
idempotency, and the cached current-pointer ids. The current
pointer fields are `null` until the corresponding engine writes
a row (decision / simulation / trust assessment / execution
plan), so callers must not assume they are populated for a
freshly-submitted intent.

current_decision_id.description: Cached pointer to the active decision envelope, if any.

current_execution_plan_id.description: Cached pointer to the active execution plan, if any.

current_simulation_id.description: Cached pointer to the active simulation report, if any.

current_trust_assessment_id.description: Cached pointer to the active trust assessment, if any.

payload_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of the submitted body.

IntentEntity.title: IntentEntity

IntentReplayResponse.description:
Full replay bundle for an intent: the original intent record,
the policy snapshot each decision referenced, the trust
assessment chain, the simulation chain, the decision envelope
chain, the execution plan chain, and the audit events. Rendered
by `BankWeb.API.V1.AuditJSON.replay/1`.

Individual item shapes (intent, policy_rule, trust_assessment,
simulation, decision, plan, audit_event) are left as permissive
objects in this foundation-level spec; per-entity sub-schemas
are a follow-up once the dedicated entity schemas are needed
elsewhere.

stablecoin_route_evidence.description:
Stablecoin route evaluations captured in the audit trail for
this intent. Each entry includes the selected provider, route
kind, policy decision, fee summary, provider errors, and the
execution-state truth (`requires_adapter` until swap/bridge
adapter dispatch is wired).

IntentReplayResponse.title: IntentReplayResponse

IntentShowResponse.description:
Response body for an intent lookup. Returns the persisted
intent record with `links` to `self` and `replay`. Decision /
simulation / plan summaries are not inlined here in v0.1 — the
cached `current_*_id` fields on `IntentEntity` point at the
active rows once the engines populate them, and full history is
available via `GET /v1/intents/{id}/replay`.
IntentShowResponse.title: IntentShowResponse

IntentState.description:
Lifecycle state of an `AgentIntent`. The flow is
`submitted → evaluating → decided → executing → executed`
on the happy path, with `blocked` and `cancelled` as
terminal side branches.
IntentState.title: IntentState

IntentSubmissionRequest.description:
Agent-supplied intent submission body. Matches the shape pinned
in `docs/bank-v0.1-runtime-flow-and-api.md`.

`idempotency_key` is required in the body even though the
contract also requires the `Idempotency-Key` header — the body
field is what the runtime persists for deterministic dedupe.
`chain` accepts the full chain enum at the schema level; the
runtime rejects non-`"base"` values at the boundary today.
IntentSubmissionRequest.title: IntentSubmissionRequest

IntentSubmitResponse.description:
Response body for a successful intent submission. Returned with
`202 Accepted`. `idempotent_replay` is `true` when the
`(agent_id, idempotency_key)` pair already existed and the
submitted body matched the original — the runtime does not write
a new intent, audit event, or evaluation job in that case.

idempotent_replay.description: True when the submission was deduped against an existing intent with the same `(agent_id, idempotency_key)` and a matching payload.

IntentSubmitResponse.title: IntentSubmitResponse

IntentTarget.description:
Target of an agent intent. The contract requires exactly one of:

  * a `counterparty_id` (optionally with `address_label_id` when
    the counterparty has multiple labels), or
  * a `raw_address`, which is always evaluated at trust `unknown`.

OpenAPI cannot perfectly express "exactly one of these two
disjoint field groups"; validation happens in `Bank.Intents` at
the runtime boundary. The shape below allows either set of fields
so tooling can describe the contract without over-constraining.
IntentTarget.title: IntentTarget

IssueTrustAssertionRequest.description:
Operator-issued trust assertion. The runtime supersedes any
prior active assertion with overlapping scope. Trust-engine-
derived assertions take the same internal shape but never come
through this endpoint — `issued_by` on the response distinguishes
the two sources.

scope.description: Optional scope object — asset / chain / amount_ceiling / time_window. Unscoped `trusted` is accepted but surfaced in the response as `coarse: true`.

IssueTrustAssertionRequest.title: IssueTrustAssertionRequest

Links.description:
Related-resource links returned alongside write responses on
the `/v1` contract (e.g. `{ "self": "/v1/intents/...", "replay":
"/v1/intents/.../replay" }`). Keys are well-known relation
names; values are relative URL strings. Callers should treat
the key set as additive — new relations may appear without
being breaking changes.
Links.title: Links

PolicyRuleEntity.description:
Policy rule as rendered by `PolicyJSON.rule/1`. `state` reflects
the row's position in the supersession chain
(`draft | active | superseded | archived`); `supersedes_id`
points at the prior version when a rule has been revised.

params.description: Rule-specific parameters. Decimal values are emitted as strings (JSON has no native decimal).

scope.description: Rule scope object (e.g. `{counterparty_id: ...}` or `{asset: "USDC"}`). Shape is rule-specific.

PolicyRuleEntity.title: PolicyRuleEntity

RevisePolicyRequest.description:
Write a new version of an active policy rule. The prior version
flips to `superseded`; in-flight evaluations continue to use
their captured snapshot. `rule_type` cannot change across a
revision (the prior value is carried forward).
RevisePolicyRequest.title: RevisePolicyRequest

reason.description: Audit-persisted reason. Defaults to `"operator_requested"` when absent.

RevokeDelegationResponse.description:
Synchronous response is a receipt — the chain-side state change
has NOT yet landed. The adapter has been asked to submit the
revoke; final state (`revoked` / `revoke_failed`) is delivered
asynchronously via the `security:events` channel and the audit
stream. Revoke is one-way at the API: re-delegation is not a v1
`/v1/security` operation.
RevokeDelegationResponse.title: RevokeDelegationResponse

SecurityPauseRequest.description:
Request body for `pause`. `reason` defaults to
`"operator_requested"`; the value is persisted to audit. See
the `scope` property for the truthful parse semantics — the
runtime does NOT reject unrecognised scope values today.

scope.description:
Pause scope. The controller parses two shapes:

  * `"counterparty:{id}"` → counterparty-scoped pause.
  * anything else (omitted, `null`, `"global"`, or any
    unrecognised value) → global pause.

The runtime does NOT currently reject unknown `scope`
values — a string that does not match
`"counterparty:{id}"` is silently treated as global. This
field is documented as a plain string rather than an enum
to stay truthful to that parse behavior. A future issue
may tighten the runtime to reject unknown values.

SecurityPauseRequest.title: SecurityPauseRequest

SecurityResumeRequest.description:
Request body for `resume`. Same `scope` parse semantics as
pause — the runtime does not reject unrecognised values.

scope.description: Resume scope. Controller recognises `"counterparty:{id}"` and treats every other value (including omitted, `"global"`, or any unrecognised string) as a global resume. Unknown values are NOT rejected at the runtime today.

SecurityResumeRequest.title: SecurityResumeRequest

SecurityStateResponse.description:
Pause / resume response. `status` carries both the successful
transition (`"paused"` / `"resumed"`) and the already-in-state
idempotent case (`"already_paused"` / `"already_running"`). The
already-in-state cases still return `200` — they are not
errors.

scope.description: Echoed scope. Always either `"global"` or `"counterparty:{id}"` — the response renders the parsed scope, so unrecognised request-side values appear here as `"global"` (see the request schemas' `scope` notes).

SecurityStateResponse.title: SecurityStateResponse

SimulationRequest.description:
Body for an on-demand simulation request. `reason` describes why
the simulation was requested; `"refresh"` resets the active
report used for decisioning.
SimulationRequest.title: SimulationRequest

Timestamp.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision. Timestamps
are runtime-authoritative: caller-supplied timestamps are
accepted only as notes metadata and never drive decisions.
Timestamp.title: Timestamp

TrustAssertionEntity.description:
Trust assertion projected by
`CounterpartyJSON.trust_assertion/1`. `coarse` is `true` when the
assertion is `trusted` and unscoped — a hint for the operator
console to ask for a tighter scope.

scope.description: Free-form scope object (asset / chain / amount_ceiling / time_window). Unscoped `trusted` is accepted but flagged as `coarse: true`.

TrustAssertionEntity.title: TrustAssertionEntity

TrustConfidence.description:
Qualitative confidence of the trust engine's assessment of a
target. `low` / `medium` / `high` map to widening-caution
behavior on downstream routing.
TrustConfidence.title: TrustConfidence

TrustLevel.description:
Derived trust level from the trust engine's assessment.
Unknown addresses (raw or otherwise unattributed) default
to `unknown`; conflicted means the evidence base disagrees
and an operator must resolve the trust state before
auto-execution can proceed.
TrustLevel.title: TrustLevel

UpdateAddressLabelRequest.description:
Patch body. The address value itself is immutable — correcting a
wrong address requires retiring this label (`retired: true`) and
attaching a new one.
UpdateAddressLabelRequest.title: UpdateAddressLabelRequest

UpdateCounterpartyRequest.description: Patch body. Every field is optional; `active: false` soft-archives the counterparty. Attaching to an archived counterparty is rejected.
UpdateCounterpartyRequest.title: UpdateCounterpartyRequest

agent_api_key.description: Placeholder for future agent API-key auth on agent-facing endpoints (`POST /v1/intents`, `GET /v1/intents/{id}`, `POST /v1/intents/{id}/simulate`). Not currently enforced on `/v1/` at runtime — declared here so later issues can attach `security: [%{"agent_api_key" => []}]` to agent operations without a second components-level change when the auth layer ships.
agent_api_key.name: X-Agent-Key

operator_bearer.description: Placeholder for future operator bearer auth. Not currently enforced on `/v1/` at runtime — today the API relies on the operator-console and network-boundary posture described in `docs/security.md`. Declared here so later issues can attach `security: [%{"operator_bearer" => []}]` to specific operations without a second components-level change when the auth layer ships.

info.description:
External control-plane API for the CryptoBank non-custodial
treasury runtime. Scoped to the public `/v1/...` surface; the
private `/internal/adapter/callback` contract is intentionally
out of scope. The authoritative prose contract for this API
lives at `docs/bank-v0.1-runtime-flow-and-api.md`.
info.title: CryptoBank /v1 API

patch.description:
Patch the label's alias / role / verified flag, or retire it.
The address value itself is immutable — wrong addresses require
retiring the label and attaching a new one.

get.description:
Returns every decision envelope currently in `approval_required`.
The `decisions` array is unpaged today; a future issue may
introduce cursor-based pagination.

post.description:
Writes a successor envelope with outcome `auto_exec`. Returns
`200` with `dispatch: "recorded"` and a `next_step` hint
pointing at the execute endpoint; v0.1 does not auto-dispatch
after approval. Requires `actor_id` in the body.
post.summary: Approve a decision in the queue
Reject a decision in the queue

get.description:
Paged, filterable audit stream. Audit events cannot be edited via
any endpoint — this list is append-only.

parameters.description: Filter by audit subject id. Typically a UUID; may be a smart-account id or on-chain address for non-intent subjects.
parameters.name: subject_id

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a prior page.
parameters.name: cursor

post.description:
v1.1 entry for the browser-native connect flow (see
`docs/wallet-connect.md`). The synchronous response is
`202 accepted` after the runtime audits the request and
enqueues `Bank.Runtime.Workers.GrantDelegation`. The worker
dispatches to the adapter; the on-chain grant + permission
artifact persistence happens via the
`delegation.state_changed{state: "granted"}` callback path.
Chain ids other than `8453` (Base) and `84532` (Base Sepolia)
return `422 unsupported_chain`.

202.description: Connect accepted (audited and enqueued for adapter dispatch)

parameters.description: Filter to active (`true`) or archived (`false`) counterparties.
parameters.name: active

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a prior page.
parameters.name: cursor

post.description: Creates a new counterparty. `name` is required; other fields are optional.

patch.description: Patch a counterparty's name / notes / active flag. `active: false` soft-archives.

post.description:
Attach a chain address to an existing counterparty. Duplicates
(same `(chain, address)` on an active label) return `409
address_already_labelled`. Attaching to an archived counterparty
returns `409 counterparty_archived`.
post.summary: Attach an address label to a counterparty

post.description:
Append a new evidence artifact to the counterparty. Evidence is
append-only: this endpoint never edits prior artifacts. Archived
counterparties reject new evidence with `409
counterparty_archived`.
post.summary: Pin an evidence artifact to a counterparty

get.description:
Returns a decision envelope's detail plus the execution plans
currently linked to it. This endpoint is live.

post.description:
Triggers execution on an `auto_exec` envelope. Used for hold
release, retry after an aborted plan, and tiered-autonomy
manual confirm. Requires `smart_account_id` in the body; the
adapter will sign with the delegation bound to that account.
Returns `202` with the new execution plan on success.

get.description:
Confirms the Postgres connection is reachable so an orchestrator
can distinguish a running web process from one that cannot serve
traffic. Returns `200` with `status: "ok"` when every check
reports `"ok"`; otherwise returns `503` with `status: "degraded"`
and the same body shape.

503.description: At least one check is degraded; body mirrors the 200 shape.

get.description:
Runs every operational check in `Bank.Ops.Health.snapshot/0`:
Postgres, adapter reachability, stuck-plan count, … Returns
`200` when every check is `ok`; otherwise `503` with a non-`ok`
overall `status`. Safe to alert on.

503.description: At least one check is degraded; body mirrors the 200 shape.

post.description:
Agent-facing entry point for submitting a structured
`AgentIntent` for evaluation. Request body fields match the
pinned contract in `docs/bank-v0.1-runtime-flow-and-api.md`.

Persists the intent in `:submitted`, audits `intent.submitted`,
and enqueues `Bank.Runtime.Workers.EvaluateIntent`. Decision /
simulation / approval engines have not yet landed, so the
enqueued job currently cancels with `:engines_pending` —
expected and visible in the Oban dashboard. Returns
`202 Accepted`.

Idempotency: a duplicate `(agent_id, idempotency_key)` with a
matching body returns the existing intent and sets
`idempotent_replay: true`; a duplicate with a mismatched body
returns `409`.

get.description:
Returns the current state of an intent together with the
cached current-pointer ids for decision / simulation / trust
assessment / execution plan.

Decision / simulation / plan summaries are not inlined here in
v0.1 — those engines have not landed yet. Callers that need
the historical chain should use `GET /v1/intents/:id/replay`.

post.description:
Operator cancellation prior to execution. Allowed while the
intent is `submitted`, `evaluating`, or `decided`; once
`executing`, operators must use security controls instead.

**Current runtime behavior: returns `501 Not Implemented`.**

get.description:
Returns a deterministic replay bundle: the original intent, the
policy snapshot each decision referenced, the trust assessment
chain, simulation chain, decision chain, execution plan chain,
and audit events. Rendered by
`BankWeb.API.V1.AuditJSON.replay/1`.

This endpoint is live today.
get.summary: Get the full replay bundle for an intent

post.description:
Produces a fresh `SimulationReport` on demand (pre-submit dry

post.description: Creates a new policy rule. `rule_type` is required; `params` / `scope` shape depends on the rule type and is validated at the context boundary.
Soft-deactivate a policy rule. Only active rules can be archived; already-superseded / already-archived rules return `409 not_active`.

Writes a new version of an active rule. The prior version is
marked `superseded`; in-flight evaluations continue using their
captured policy snapshot. `rule_type` cannot change across a
revision. Archived or already-superseded rules return `409
not_active`.

Soft pause — blocks new `executing` transitions while letting
pending confirmations keep polling, agents keep submitting, and
decisions keep being written.

Scope parse: `"counterparty:{id}"` yields a counterparty-scoped
pause; any other value (omitted, `null`, `"global"`, or an
unrecognised string) is currently treated as a global pause —
the runtime does NOT reject unknown scope values today. See
`SecurityPauseRequest.scope` for the truthful wording.

The already-paused case returns `200` with
`status: "already_paused"` — it is idempotent, not an error.

Lifts the pause. Intents that accumulated while paused are NOT
auto-flushed into execution — each still needs a decision event
or a manual `POST /v1/decisions/{id}/execute`.

Scope parse: same semantics as pause — `"counterparty:{id}"`
resumes that scope, any other value resumes globally. The
runtime does NOT reject unknown `scope` values today. Returns
`200` with `status: "already_running"` when the scope was not
paused.

Enqueues a delegation revoke for the given smart account. The
synchronous response is a **receipt**: `202 revoke_enqueued`
with the `smart_account_id` as the handle. The chain-side state
change has NOT yet landed — final state is delivered
asynchronously via the `security:events` realtime channel and
the audit stream.

Revoke is one-way at the API: re-delegation is intentionally
not a v1 `/v1/security` operation. Re-delegation is an operator
flow in the web console's security surface, outside the
external API.

Operator-issued manual trust override. Any prior active
assertion with overlapping scope is marked `superseded`.
Trust-engine-derived assertions take the same internal shape
but never come through this endpoint; the response's
`issued_by` disambiguates.
